overview: Black plays ...d6 against the Nf3 set-up, heading for an Old Indian or King's Indian-type structure or for ...Nbd7 and ...e5. White usually plays 3.Bg5 or 3.g3, or c4 and Nc3 to reach a King's Indian. Play is flexible and mostly transposes to other Indian structures.

white_ideas.idea: 3.Bg5 and e3/Nbd7 or c4 and Nc3 to take space against a flexible Black set-up
3.g3 with a fianchetto and c4, aiming for a slight space edge

black_ideas.idea: ...Nbd7 and ...e5 or ...g6 and ...Bg7 for a King's Indian structure
Delay committing the centre and respond to White's choice of set-up

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian or Old Indian structures with ...d6 and ...e5, depending on White's set-up

character.notes: Not forcing; flexible with room for both sides. I am unsure of the main line.

structure.notes: Not yet decided; transposes into many structures.

approach.notes: Played by some strong players as a move-order choice; respectable.

level.notes: Needs understanding of King's Indian-style plans but little theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.Bg5 Nbd7
sublines_that_differ.how: Heading for ...e5 with an Old Indian set-up and Black not committing the bishop.

character.reason: Flexible and not forcing; neither especially sharp nor rigid.

structure.reason: Centre is undecided and the move order transposes.

approach.reason: A normal if less common route into Indian set-ups.

level.reason: Plans need understanding but there is little theory.

plans.reason: Black lets White build a centre, then attacks it with ...e5 or ...c5.
